goal: Cut token usage. rlo-sdk gets prompt-spec/1, a semantic signature for one LLM task that marks its static and per-turn parts. It also gets a deterministic compiler with a verbatim mode and a compact mode, an output checker built from the same spec, and a per-section token report. There is no optimizer and there are no model calls.
why: POL-2 T1, CMD-AO3 rev 3 (BD-288/289/290). The user dropped prompt optimization ('let's not do prompt optimization'); the goal is fewer tokens for the same checked output. Today prompts are hand-written str.format text, and hosts without --resume (agy) resend protocol() and the task on every turn. T2 (GA moves the ga gemini plan prompt onto this) is issued only after T1 is judged.
refs: baseline SEMANTIC_MODEL.md section 1 (Opinion has no authority; terms)
ga-sdk 438a34a ga/gemini.py _prompt() and protocol() (the T2 consumer; read only)

scope.text: prompt-spec/1: a versioned, validated data form for one LLM task: goal; inputs, each with a name, a SEMANTIC_MODEL term (Observation, State, Evidence, DecisionContext, ...) and a basis; one output form with typed fields; rules; optional examples; and, for each part, whether it is static (sent once per conversation) or per-turn. Unknown terms, a missing basis, or a part with no static/per-turn mark are validation errors. The answer is an Opinion (SEMANTIC_MODEL section 1), never State.

Compiler: (spec, inputs, mode, turn) -> prompt text, deterministic and byte-stable for the same input on any OS (no dict order, time, locale or random dependence). verbatim mode reproduces a given hand-written text exactly, which proves that a conversion loses nothing. compact mode sends static parts only on the first turn, uses short field names, and drops prose that the output checker does not need. Both modes ask for the same output form.
The output checker (parse + validate the answer) is built from the same spec, so the prompt and its parser cannot drift. It accepts the same well-formed answer whichever mode produced the prompt.

Token report per compiled prompt: tokens per section (static, per-turn, examples) and the total, using one documented offline estimator that is deterministic and needs no network or download. When a caller passes the provider's real usage (from Telemetry), the report shows it next to the estimate. Report verbatim and compact side by side for a given turn sequence.

No optimizer: no variant search, no LLM-scored metric, no model calls, no provider SDK import, no keys and no built-in quota. Any optimizer code written for rev 1 or rev 2 stays off the integration branch (keep it on a side branch if you want, and name it in the report).

done_when.text: Compiler: verbatim output is byte-identical to a hand-written fixture text, twice and from a fresh process. compact is shorter than verbatim on every follow-up turn of a multi-turn fixture and contains no static section after turn 1. A spec that fails S1 validation is rejected. Mutations killed: static resent in compact on turn 2 or later, field order taken from a set or dict, verbatim off by one byte, unknown SEMANTIC_MODEL term accepted.

Checker and token report: the checker from the spec accepts the well-formed answer for both modes and rejects a malformed one. The section counts sum to the total and are identical across runs. A passed real usage appears next to the estimate. Mutations killed: checker built from a different spec, a section dropped from the count, estimator dependent on dict order.

Minor version bump. An empty venv installs rlo-sdk at your commit with a clean pip check. The full suite passes in a fresh clone, with 0 network calls and 0 model calls. No optimizer code is on the integration branch. Report as report/2 in English on #11 with the commit sha, the verbatim versus compact token numbers for the fixture, and a short API sketch for GA (T2).
